collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 40 or older)

collection.description: Watching a wedding, a villager thinks about their own choices: raise a cup to the couple, or slip away for a while.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: There's a wedding today, and (name1) is watching from the back with a cup of something sweet. The couple are tying the cord around their wrists, laughing at how long it's taking. (name1) finds (him/her)self thinking about (his/her) own choices: who (he/she) loved, who (he/she) didn't, what (he/she) did about it, and what (he/she) didn't.

choices.label: Raise a Cup to the Couple

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (name1) slips away and walks along the beach in the evening light. The music fades behind (him/her). (He/she) thinks about the roads (he/she) took and the ones (he/she) didn't. (He/she) doesn't feel sad, exactly. Wistful. Full. When (he/she) comes back, the dancing has started, and (he/she) joins in. Some feelings don't need deciding about.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (name1) raises (his/her) cup to the couple, and means it. Whatever (his/her) own life has held, (he/she) hopes theirs is good. The couple see it and raise their tied hands. (name1) feels a twinge of something, maybe longing, maybe relief, maybe both, and lets it be. Then (he/she) goes and dances very badly with an elder. It's a lovely wedding.
